script.base: Spread and total are not in the pack, so this is form-only. Detroit has been the engine (Gibbs 45 carries for 208, St. Brown 27 targets for 209) and the Jets defense the brake (4.09 YPC allowed, 1 pass of 20+ on 67 attempts). Base flow: DET controls on the ground with Gibbs, keeps the pass game on St. Brown's volume rather than explosives, and NYJ uses Breece Hall as runner and checkdown instead of a vertical game.
script.flip1: NYJ's defense (only 4 runs of 10+, 1 explosive pass) turns it into a slog: Gibbs's efficiency falls toward the 4.09 YPC NYJ allows, DET never pulls away, and Hall keeps a full carry share instead of being scripted out.
script.flip2: DET's 43% blitz and 13.27 middle YPA let the Jets QB (0.18 EPA both blitzed and not, n=20) hit the middle in a higher-scoring game; Hall's checkdowns spike and Jameson Williams's deep shots (177 air yards in two games) finally connect.

injury_fallout: No injury report, practice trend, or inactives in the pack, so no next-man-up can be assigned and a late scratch would need a re-run. Weeks 1-2 roles stand: Hall 38 carries/131 and 7 targets/79 rec yards; Allen 15/47 with no targets listed, a rush complement not a receiving thief; St. Brown 27 targets; Gibbs 45 carries and 13 targets; LaPorta 15 targets/100 yards; Jameson Williams 13 targets on 177 air yards. Vaki (3/14) is not a Gibbs replacement without an injury that is not in the pack.

matchup.shell: Man/zone and MOFO/MOFC charting are not in the pack. Location YPA only: DET allows left 4.11 (27 att), middle 13.27 (15 att), right 7.91 (44 att). NYJ allows left 5.73 (22), middle 5.91 (11), right 3.36 (28).
matchup.pressure: DET blitzes 43%. NYJ QB EPA/dropback is 0.18 vs blitz (n=20) and 0.18 without, so the blitz does not collapse the dropback and should funnel quick throws to Hall (2 air yards on 7 targets). NYJ blitzes only 28%; Goff is better vs the blitz (0.33 EPA, n=23) than without (0.18), so Jets pressure is not a path to killing Detroit's skill players.
matchup.bleeds: DET run defense allows 5.12 YPC and 10 runs of 10+, plus 10 passes of 20+ on 94 attempts; the middle at 13.27 YPA is the pass bleed. NYJ is the opposite: 4.09 YPC, 4 runs of 10+, and 1 pass of 20+ on 67 attempts, with no zone above 5.91 YPA.
matchup.overlap: Hall is the overlap: a 3.45 YPC back who can be more efficient into a 5.12 YPC, 10-explosive run defense, and a zero-air-yard receiver against a 43% blitz that already leaks the middle. St. Brown (13.5 targets per game) has no mapped weak spot — NYJ's worst zone is still 5.91 YPA. Jameson Williams's 177 air yards overlap the one thing NYJ has taken away (1/67 explosives).

edge_players.edge_sentence: Detroit allows 5.12 yards per carry and 10 runs of 10-plus while blitzing 43% and giving up 13.27 YPA in the middle, and Hall already has 105 rush-plus-receiving yards per game (38/131 rushing, 7 targets/79 receiving) against an 86 line, so the run matchup or the checkdown role can clear it.
edge_players.must_be_true: Hall keeps the weeks 1-2 role, about 19 carries and the Jets' RB targets (Allen has 15 carries but no listed targets), on a full snap share, and Detroit's run leak or 43% blitz shows up again.
edge_players.kills_it: NYJ falls way behind, Allen takes the remaining carries, and Hall's 79 receiving yards were one screen we cannot verify (2 air yards, no play log), or a snap limit that is invisible because inactives are not in the pack.

edge_players.edge_sentence: Jameson Williams is the shot player (13 targets, 78 yards, 177 air yards, 39 per game) and the Jets have allowed one 20-plus pass on 67 attempts, so a 54-yard line sits above both his production and what this defense gives up.
edge_players.must_be_true: NYJ's explosive suppression holds and St. Brown (27 targets, 209 yards) stays the volume receiver so Jameson does not inherit a 10-target intermediate role.
edge_players.kills_it: The shootout flip: one busted coverage, which is his whole profile (177 air yards for 78 yards), clears 54 by itself if DET trails and opens the deep shots.

data_check.notes: No projection, sim median, or Pinnacle no-vig in the pack; Hall rush+rec over 86 and Jameson recyds under 54 are both priced +nan, so nothing to size to a sharp number. Counting data agrees with both reads: Hall 131+79=210 over two games (105/game vs 86), backed by DET 5.12 YPC and a 43% blitz; Jameson 78 yards on 13 targets (39/game) vs 54, backed by NYJ 1/67 explosives. Do not treat either as a 70%+ leg on a two-game sample. No disagreeing number strong enough to flag the Hall read.

market_rung_price: Hall rushrecyds over 86 (price not in pack, +nan), not the thinner rushyds 60 (65.5 per game, dies if NYJ trails) and not recyds 21.5 (a single screen can own it). Jameson Williams recyds under 54 (price +nan). No alt rungs in the pack. No short-priced alts.
pre_mortem: Monday, Hall lost because the 79 receiving yards were one long screen and Allen's 15 carries became the clock-kill share while Hall's 3.45 YPC stuck — that is a Jets line problem, not something Detroit's 5.12 YPC allowed automatically fixes — so 12 carries at 3.2 plus a quiet receiving day lands near 50, well under 86. Jameson lost on one 40-yard shot in a game DET had to throw. No inactives in the pack, so an unseen Hall snap limit is an unpriced kill. That counter-case is real but not stronger than Hall's two-path cushion (105 vs 86) or Jameson's explosives mismatch, so both stay and Jameson stays a lean only.
slip_story: One story: Detroit controls without a shootout. The Jets' defense keeps the lid on (Jameson recyds under 54) while Detroit's leaky run defense and 43% blitz still feed Hall as runner and checkdown (rushrecyds over 86). Do not add St. Brown, Gibbs, or Wilson overs or a game over — those need the shootout flip that kills the Jameson leg. No TDs, no receptions, one market per player.
